title: Answering a Rude Remark
short: Stay calm; ask "Why do you ask?", give a short neutral answer, change the subject, or simply say "I'd rather not discuss that."
trouble: Learners answer rudeness with rudeness or feel they must answer a nosy question. You never owe a personal answer; a calm deflection keeps your dignity.

blocks.html: Sometimes the rude one is someone else. You learned to handle other people's slips kindly; a rude remark or a nosy question calls for the same calm.
Stay calm. Ask "Why do you ask?", give a short neutral answer, change the subject, or simply say, "I'd rather not discuss that." You never owe a personal answer.

Answering rudeness with rudeness makes two rude people instead of one, and it often feeds the argument. A calm reply keeps your dignity and usually ends the moment. A nosy question, about money, weight, age, or why you are not married or have no children, is not owed an answer: a polite deflection protects your privacy without starting a fight.

head: The remark
A calm reply
rows: "Enough! But we love it. Have you been to the new park nearby?"
"Why do you ask?" or "That's not something I discuss, but thank you."
"I'd rather not talk about that." Then change the subject.
"It's a favorite of mine. Would you like to try some?"

blocks.title: A nosy question
blocks.q: At a family dinner, a relative asks Priya, "How much do you make at that new job?" She would rather not say. What can she answer?
steps: She doesn't owe a personal answer.
She smiles and says, "Enough to keep me happy! I love the work, though. We're building a new library app."
The short answer and the new topic move things along.
blocks.a: A light, short answer and a change of subject.

blocks.title: A pointed remark
blocks.q: A coworker says to Kofi in a meeting, "That's a pretty basic idea." What is a calm reply?
steps: He stays calm and doesn't trade insults.
"Maybe! Simple ideas are sometimes the ones that work. What would you change?"
Inviting a better idea turns the remark back into a discussion.
blocks.a: Stay calm and invite the other person's idea.

cards.why: It makes two rude people instead of one.
You never owe a personal answer; short and calm is enough.

cards.text: Changing the subject with a smile

blocks.html: Answering rudeness with rudeness, or feeling you must answer a nosy question. You never owe a personal answer; a calm deflection keeps your dignity. If someone keeps pressing, it is fine to excuse yourself and walk away.
